answer: Before funding a sparrow survey in a grove beside a lagoon, freeze a stake snapshot and use a future random beacon to draw numbered stake units as committee seats. Each unit gets one ticket, regardless of its owner's accounts. Transfers or new keys after the snapshot create no tickets; duplicate claims on a winning unit are rejected. Splitting S units among n aliases still yields S tickets. Greater influence requires acquiring or renting more stake before the freeze. Unpredictable randomness and unbiased sampling are essential; wealth concentration remains a risk.
